lines.text: For such as have experienced "that day", prayer of this
character is a matter of course. For these are they who have
penetrated to that centre of life where they are alone in the
presence of God, and this loneliness itself becomes for them
a prayer. True prayer in the name of Jesus implies that with
Him we enter consoledly the region of solitary encounter
with God, in whose sight we are aware of standing and by
whom we allow ourselves to be confronted. "In the world
you have tribulation; but be of good cheer, I have overcome
the world." This solitariness of the soul can itself become a
prayer, a cry of the heart for God:
"It may be that I pierce through rugged mountain sides,
through harsh veins, like ore, alone; so deep I delve that
I see no end, no distant view; all has become near, all near-
ness hard as stone. Yet I am not experienced in the ways of
sorrow, and this entombing darkness makes me small. But
Thou art; may the weight of Thy glory burst upon me, the
weight of Thy whole hand smite me, and I with all my
treasure fall prostrate before Thee."1
Of such prayer it is true to say: "In prayer we rise to Him
as from the bands of death. Sorely our heart needed His
breath which breathed around us." 2
Whoever practises such prayers goes back to the round of
daily life, comforted and thankful that with all the impulses
of his heart he may open himself to God without reserve.
Such a one will be accompanied by the prayer of solitude
in all life's encounters; it will impart to him that freedom and
joy in the inspiration of which he will no longer need to ask
questions.
In conclusion let us think of those words of Paul: "Three
times I besought the Lord about this... but He said to me
'My grace is sufficient for you, for my power is made perfect
in weakness.' " Was this an answer to his prayer or not?
Paul understood it to be an answer: "I will all the more
gladly boast of my weaknesses, that the power of Christ may
rest upon me. For the sake of Christ, then, I am content with
weaknesses, insults, hardships, persecutions, and calamities;
1 R. M. Rilke.
2 A. v. Arnim.
